question.:question/problem: A farmer estimates that she can sell $w(p)$ metric tons of crops at a price of $p$ dollars per ton. What are the units of $\frac{dw}{dp}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have that $w(p)$ is measured in tons and $p$ is measured in dollars per ton. 

$$
\begin{aligned}w(p): & \text{tons} \\ p: & \text{dollars per ton}\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative $\frac{\text{d}w}{\text{d}p}$ measures a change in $w(p)$ over a change in $p.$ So, it represents a ratio of the units:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}w}{\text{d}p}: & \frac{\text{tons}}{\text{dollars per ton}}=\frac{\text{squared tons}}{\text{dollars}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\frac{\text{d}w}{\text{d}p}$ is measured in "squared tons per dollar".
